examples.ko: 남편이 성공한 데에는 아내의 내조가 컸어요.
examples.en: His wife's support played a big part in her husband's success.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 부인의 내조 덕분에 선거에서 이겼어요.
examples.en: That politician won the election thanks to his wife's support.

examples.ko: 요즘은 내조보다 서로 돕는다는 말을 더 많이 써요.
examples.en: These days people say 'helping each other' more than 'naejo'.

examples.ko: 어머니는 평생 아버지를 위해 내조를 하며 사셨어요.
examples.en: My mother spent her whole life supporting my father behind the scenes.

examples.ko: 내조의 여왕이라는 말을 들으면 기분이 어때요?
examples.en: How would you feel if people called you the queen of spousal support?

examples.ko: 회사 대표의 부인은 조용한 내조로 유명해요.
examples.en: The company president's wife is known for her quiet support.

explain: 남편의 일을 아내가 뒤에서 돕는 것에 써요. 반대로 남편이 아내를 돕는 것은 '외조'라고 해요. 요즘은 역할을 나누는 느낌 때문에 일상에서는 '뒷받침하다', '도와주다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '내조의 여왕'은 방송과 기사에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used when a wife helps her husband's work from behind the scenes. The reverse, a husband helping his wife, is '외조'. Because it implies divided gender roles, people now say '뒷받침하다' or '도와주다' in daily talk, while '내조의 여왕' still appears often in TV and news.

examples.en: The long journey of preparing for the Olympics has finally begun.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 전국 투어 대장정을 마치고 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: The singer came back after finishing a long nationwide tour.

examples.ko: 십 년간의 대장정 끝에 책이 완성됐어요.
examples.en: After a ten-year-long effort, the book was completed.
The players set out on the long road toward the championship.
This long journey was really long and hard.
We safely finished the long journey that was shooting the film.

explain: 실제 먼 길뿐 아니라 오래 걸리고 힘든 큰 일이나 프로젝트를 비유할 때 많이 써요. '대장정에 오르다/나서다', '대장정을 마치다'처럼 짝지어 쓰고, 가벼운 여행에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: Besides a literal long trek, it is often used figuratively for a big, long, demanding project. It pairs with '대장정에 오르다/나서다' and '대장정을 마치다', and it is not used for a light trip.

examples.en: This novel is a representative work of realist literature.
We learned about realist painters in art class.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 리얼리즘을 잘 살려서 현실처럼 느껴져요.
examples.en: That film makes good use of realism, so it feels like real life.
How are realism and romanticism different?
This director is famous for his realist techniques.

examples.ko: 리얼리즘이 강한 드라마라서 보기 불편할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: The drama is so realistic that it is sometimes uncomfortable to watch.

explain: 문학, 미술, 영화 수업이나 평론에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '현실적이다', '리얼하다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. 함께 배우는 말로 '낭만주의'가 있어요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in literature, art and film classes and in criticism. In everyday talk people more often say '현실적이다' or '리얼하다'. '낭만주의' (romanticism) is a term you often learn alongside it.

examples.en: Seoraksan is one of Korea's most famous mountains.
Every weekend I visit famous mountains around the country.

examples.ko: 이 지역에는 이름난 명산이 많아서 등산객이 와요.
examples.en: This area has many well-known mountains, so hikers come.

examples.ko: 아버지는 명산 사진 찍는 걸 좋아하세요.
examples.en: My father likes taking photos of famous mountains.

examples.ko: 명산으로 알려진 곳이라 사람이 정말 많았어요.
examples.en: It is known as a famous mountain, so there were really a lot of people.

examples.ko: 가을에는 명산마다 단풍 구경하는 사람들로 붐벼요.
examples.en: In autumn every famous mountain is crowded with people viewing the leaves.

explain: 등산이나 여행 이야기에서 '전국의 명산', '○○ 명산'처럼 써요. 대화에서는 '유명한 산'이라고 더 자주 말해요. 산뿐 아니라 이름난 장소 전체는 '명소'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used in hiking and travel talk, as in '전국의 명산' or 'OO 명산'. In conversation people more often say '유명한 산'. For famous places in general, the word is '명소'.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 박력 있는 목소리로 연기해요.
examples.en: That actor performs with a powerful voice.

examples.ko: 팀장님은 박력이 넘쳐서 일을 빠르게 밀어붙여요.
examples.en: Our team leader is full of drive and pushes work forward fast.
The presentation lacked punch, which was a pity.
Try doing it with some energy!

examples.ko: 박력 있는 춤을 보고 관객이 환호했어요.
examples.en: The audience cheered at the energetic dance.

examples.ko: 그의 박력에 눌려서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was overwhelmed by his forcefulness and couldn't say anything.

explain: '박력 있다/넘치다/없다'로 많이 써요. 사람의 태도, 목소리, 연기, 영상처럼 힘차게 밀고 나가는 기세를 말할 때 쓰고, 보통 칭찬이에요. 몸의 힘을 말하는 '힘'과는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '박력 있다/넘치다/없다'. It describes a forceful, driving presence in a person's attitude, voice, acting or visuals, and is usually a compliment. It differs from '힘', which refers to physical strength.

examples.ko: 학교 앞길에 벚나무가 쭉 심어져 있어요.
examples.en: Cherry trees are planted all along the road in front of the school.

examples.ko: 봄이 되면 벚나무에 꽃이 활짝 펴요.
examples.en: When spring comes, the cherry trees bloom fully.
The street trees in my neighborhood are cherry trees.
We ate a packed lunch with my family under a cherry tree.
The cherry tree leaves have already turned red.

examples.ko: 이 벚나무는 나이가 백 년이 넘었대요.
examples.en: I heard this cherry tree is over a hundred years old.

explain: 꽃은 '벚꽃', 나무는 '벚나무'로 나눠 말해요. 봄에 꽃을 보러 가는 것은 '벚꽃 구경'이나 '벚꽃놀이'라고 해요. 소리는 [번나무]로 나요.
explain_en: The blossom is '벚꽃' and the tree is '벚나무'. Going to see the blossoms in spring is called '벚꽃 구경' or '벚꽃놀이'. It is pronounced [번나무].

examples.en: He suffered for a long time because of his desire for revenge.

examples.ko: 복수심에 불타서 아무것도 눈에 안 들어왔어요.
examples.en: Burning with revenge, I couldn't see anything else.
Nothing gets solved by a thirst for revenge.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 복수심을 품고 살아가요.
examples.en: The hero of the movie lives holding a grudge and a desire for revenge.
Once my desire for revenge faded, I felt much more at ease.

examples.ko: 그의 마음에는 복수심만 가득 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Only a desire for revenge is left in his heart.

explain: '복수하다'가 행동이라면 '복수심'은 마음이에요. '복수심에 불타다', '복수심을 품다/키우다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 대화보다는 영화, 드라마, 기사 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: While '복수하다' is the act, '복수심' is the feeling. It pairs as '복수심에 불타다' and '복수심을 품다/키우다'. It shows up more in talk about movies, dramas and news than in casual conversation.

examples.en: A snail leaves a secretion where it has crawled.

examples.ko: 눈에 분비물이 많이 나와서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: A lot of discharge came out of my eye, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 이 식물은 잎에서 나오는 분비물로 벌레를 쫓아요.
examples.en: This plant drives off insects with a secretion from its leaves.

examples.ko: 상처에서 노란 분비물이 계속 나오면 의사에게 보여 주세요.
examples.en: If yellow discharge keeps coming out of the wound, show it to a doctor.

examples.ko: 고양이 털과 분비물 때문에 알레르기가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get allergies from cat hair and secretions.
I took a class that studies animal secretions.

explain: 눈곱, 콧물, 땀, 침처럼 몸에서 나오는 것을 묶어서 부르는 말이에요. 병원이나 생물 수업에서 많이 쓰고, 일상에서는 '눈곱', '콧물'처럼 구체적으로 말해요. 동사는 '분비되다'예요.
explain_en: It is a collective term for things that come out of a body, such as eye gunk, snot, sweat and saliva. It is common at hospitals and in biology class, while in daily life people name the specific thing like '눈곱' or '콧물'. The related verb is '분비되다'.

examples.en: Pork belly tastes greasy if it has too much fat.
I cut the fat off the meat before eating.

examples.ko: 비계 부분이 고소해서 좋아하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people like the fatty part because it is rich and nutty.

examples.ko: 돼지고기 비계에서 기름을 내서 볶음밥에 써요.
examples.en: I render oil from pork fat and use it for fried rice.
Please give me only the lean meat and leave out the fat.
Don't leave just the fat, eat it all.

explain: 주로 돼지고기나 소고기에서 말하고, 반대말은 '살코기'예요. 식당이나 정육점에서 '비계 빼 주세요'처럼 자주 말해요. 건설 현장의 '비계'는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to the fat on pork or beef, and its opposite is '살코기' (lean meat). You often hear '비계 빼 주세요' at restaurants and butcher shops. The '비계' used at construction sites is a different word that only sounds the same.

examples.en: If you rub the wood surface with sandpaper, it gets smooth.
The sandpaper is rough, so my hand hurts.
I bought sandpaper to strip off the paint.
I sanded for a long time, so my arm hurts.

examples.ko: 사포 번호가 높을수록 더 곱게 갈려요.
examples.en: The higher the sandpaper number, the finer it sands.

examples.ko: 이 사포는 철에도 쓸 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can this sandpaper be used on metal too?

explain: 가구, 벽, 나무를 매끈하게 다듬을 때 써요. '사포질하다', '사포로 갈다/문지르다'처럼 말하고, 가게에서는 번호로 거칠기를 말해요.
explain_en: It is used to smooth furniture, walls and wood. People say '사포질하다' or '사포로 갈다/문지르다', and in shops the roughness is given by a number.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 송전이 끊겨서 마을이 어두워졌어요.
examples.en: The power transmission was cut by the typhoon, so the village went dark.

examples.ko: 산에 송전탑을 세우는 문제로 주민들이 반대해요.
examples.en: Residents are opposing the plan to build power transmission towers on the mountain.

examples.ko: 발전소에서 도시까지 송전하는 데 선이 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: Many lines are needed to transmit power from the plant to the city.
There was a blackout because they were inspecting the transmission facilities.

examples.ko: 먼 곳으로 송전할 때 전기가 조금 손실돼요.
examples.en: Some electricity is lost when transmitting it over long distances.
Work on the power transmission lines starts tomorrow.

explain: 집에서는 '전기가 들어오다/끊기다'라고 하고, '송전'은 뉴스와 공사 이야기에서 써요. '송전탑', '송전선', '송전 중단'처럼 합쳐서 자주 나와요. 전기를 만드는 '발전'과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: At home people say '전기가 들어오다/끊기다', while '송전' belongs to news and construction talk. It often appears in compounds like '송전탑', '송전선' and '송전 중단'. It helps to remember it as a pair with '발전' (generating power).

examples.ko: 이 소설은 그냥 습작이라서 아직 보여 주기 부끄러워요.
examples.en: This novel is just a practice piece, so I'm embarrassed to show it yet.

examples.ko: 대학 때 쓴 습작을 서랍에서 찾았어요.
examples.en: I found a piece I wrote as practice in college in a drawer.

examples.ko: 그 화가의 초기 습작들이 전시되고 있어요.
examples.en: The painter's early studies are on display.

examples.ko: 습작 시절에는 매일 한 편씩 시를 썼어요.
examples.en: In my apprentice days I wrote one poem every day.

examples.ko: 습작 노트를 보면 그 작가의 고민이 느껴져요.
examples.en: Looking at the practice notebook, you can feel the author's struggles.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 큰 작품을 위한 습작이에요.
examples.en: This painting is a study for a larger work.

explain: 완성작이 아니라 연습이나 준비 단계의 작품이라는 느낌이 있어요. '습작기', '습작 시절'처럼 쓰고, 시, 소설, 그림에 주로 써요. 일상에서는 '연습으로 쓴 글'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of a work made as practice or preparation rather than a finished piece. It appears in phrases like '습작기' and '습작 시절' and is mostly used for poems, novels and paintings. In daily talk people also say '연습으로 쓴 글'.

examples.ko: 그는 고등학생 때부터 시를 습작해 왔어요.
examples.en: He has been writing practice poems since high school.

examples.ko: 매일 밤 소설을 습작하면서 작가를 꿈꿨어요.
examples.en: Every night I practiced writing novels and dreamed of being an author.

examples.ko: 습작하는 동안 선생님께 여러 번 조언을 들었어요.
examples.en: While I was writing practice pieces, I got advice from my teacher many times.
It's fine to make mistakes when you're doing practice drawings.

examples.ko: 친구와 같이 희곡을 습작해 보기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to try writing a practice play with a friend.
I'm attached to it because it's a piece I practiced on for a long time.

explain: '시를 습작하다', '소설을 습작하다'처럼 글이나 그림을 목적어로 해서 써요. '연습하다'와 달리 창작에만 써서 대화에서는 드물고 글에서 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It takes writing or drawing as its object, as in '시를 습작하다' or '소설을 습작하다'. Unlike '연습하다', it is limited to creative work, so it is rare in conversation and more common in writing.

examples.en: I thought it over carefully before deciding to move.
After careful consideration, I decided to change companies.
It's an important matter, so please answer after careful thought.

examples.ko: 너무 오래 심사숙고하면 기회를 놓칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you deliberate too long, you may miss the chance.
Our team leader is the deliberating type, so decisions are slow.
I regret speaking without thinking it through.

explain: '고민하다'보다 격식 있고, 충분히 따져 본 끝에 결론을 낸다는 쪽이라 면접, 회의, 글에서 잘 써요. '심사숙고 끝에', '심사숙고 후에'처럼 자주 말해요. 짧게 '숙고하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '고민하다' and suggests reaching a conclusion after thoroughly weighing things, so it suits interviews, meetings and writing. Forms like '심사숙고 끝에' and '심사숙고 후에' are very common. It can be shortened to '숙고하다'.

examples.en: My uncle keeps bees in the countryside.
They get honey from beekeeping and sell it.
Why is the number of beekeeping farms increasing?
I signed up for a beekeeping experience class.
When honeybees decrease, people who keep bees have a hard time.

examples.ko: 양봉장에 가려면 보호 옷을 입어야 해요.
examples.en: To go to an apiary, you have to wear protective clothing.

explain: '양봉을 하다'로 많이 쓰고, 하는 사람은 '양봉업자', 장소는 '양봉장'이라고 해요. 일상에서는 '벌을 치다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '양봉을 하다'; the person is a '양봉업자' and the place is a '양봉장'. In daily speech people also say '벌을 치다'.

examples.en: He has such fine character that everyone respects him.
A person's character shows in small actions.
I want to be like my teacher in character.

examples.ko: 인품 좋은 사장님 밑에서 일해서 행복해요.
examples.en: I'm happy working under a boss with a good character.

examples.ko: 실력도 중요하지만 인품만 보고 뽑기도 해요.
examples.en: Skill matters, but sometimes they hire based on character alone.

examples.ko: 인품도 갖춘 사람이 리더가 되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope someone with good character as well becomes the leader.

explain: 성격 중에서도 사람됨과 품위를 평가하는 말이라 '인품이 좋다/훌륭하다/높다'처럼 좋은 쪽에 써요. 그냥 성격을 말할 때는 '성격'이 더 자연스러워요. 존경하는 어른이나 윗사람 이야기에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It evaluates a person's character and dignity, so it is used on the positive side, as in '인품이 좋다/훌륭하다/높다'. For plain personality, '성격' sounds more natural. It fits talk about respected elders or superiors.

examples.en: Let's wrap up here for now and take a break.

examples.ko: 보고서 작성은 일단락 지었으니 이제 발표를 준비해요.
examples.en: I've finished the report for now, so I'm preparing the presentation.

examples.ko: 이 일이 일단락이 되면 같이 여행 가요.
examples.en: When this work is wrapped up, let's go on a trip together.

examples.ko: 오늘 일은 여기서 일단락으로 하고 퇴근해요.
examples.en: Let's call today's work done here and go home.
I accepted the apology and put the matter to rest.

examples.ko: 공사가 일단락은 됐지만 마무리 청소가 남았어요.
examples.en: The construction is done for now, but the final cleaning remains.

explain: 대부분 '일단락 짓다', '일단락이 되다'처럼 써요. 완전히 끝났다기보다 한 고비를 넘겼다는 느낌이라 뒤에 '아직 할 일이 남았다'가 이어질 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '일단 마무리하다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '일단락 짓다' or '일단락이 되다'. It feels less like totally finished and more like getting past one stage, so 'but there is still work left' can follow. In daily talk people also say '일단 마무리하다'.

en: come to an end; be completed; end

examples.en: The long conflict was settled for now by this agreement.

examples.ko: 공사가 일단락돼서 이제 좀 쉬어도 돼요.
examples.en: The construction has reached a stopping point, so I can rest a little now.
The controversy seemed to be settling, but it grew again.
I'll contact you once this issue is wrapped up.
Even after the election was over, the talk went on.
Once the exams were over, I watched a movie with friends.

explain: 사건, 논란, 작업이 한 단계 정리될 때 써요. 완전히 끝난 게 아니라 일단 한숨 돌린다는 느낌이에요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 일이고, 사람이 하면 '일단락 짓다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when an incident, controversy or task gets settled at one stage. It means catching your breath rather than being completely finished. The subject is the matter, not a person; when a person does it, you say '일단락 짓다'.

examples.en: The enlistment notice came to my house.
My enlistment date has been set, so my feelings are mixed.

examples.ko: 입영을 앞두고 친구들이 송별회를 열어 줬어요.
examples.en: With my enlistment coming up, my friends threw me a farewell party.
I want to go on a trip before enlisting.
I decided to take time off school because of my enlistment.

examples.ko: 입영 연기를 신청하려면 어떻게 해야 해요?
examples.en: What do I have to do to apply to postpone enlistment?

explain: '입영 통지서', '입영 날짜', '입영 연기'처럼 합쳐서 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '군대 가다'가 더 흔하고, 같은 상황에서 '입대'라는 말도 써요. 군대를 마치고 나오는 것은 '제대'나 '전역'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It appears in compounds like '입영 통지서', '입영 날짜' and '입영 연기'. In daily talk '군대 가다' is more common, and '입대' is also used for the same situation. Finishing service is called '제대' or '전역'.

examples.en: My younger brother enlists next week.
I enlisted after finishing my second year of university.
I cut my hair short before enlisting.

examples.ko: 친구가 입영한 뒤로 편지를 자주 써요.
examples.en: I write letters often since my friend enlisted.
My parents saw me off on the day I enlisted.
I couldn't enlist because my health was poor.

explain: 병무청 같은 공식 안내와 뉴스에서 자주 쓰고, 대화에서는 '군대 가다'가 더 흔해요. 같은 상황의 '입대하다'도 써요. 반대로 군 생활을 마치는 것은 '제대하다'예요.
explain_en: It is common in official notices such as from the Military Manpower Administration and in the news, while '군대 가다' is more common in conversation. '입대하다' is also used for the same situation. Finishing service is '제대하다'.

examples.en: I get starch from potatoes and use it in cooking.

examples.ko: 탕수육 소스는 전분 물을 넣어서 걸쭉하게 만들어요.
examples.en: You thicken sweet and sour sauce by adding starch water.
Rice contains a lot of starch.

examples.ko: 전분 가루가 없으면 밀가루로 대신해도 돼요?
examples.en: If I don't have starch powder, can I use flour instead?
Noodles made from potato starch are chewy.

examples.ko: 전분은 찬물에 잘 안 녹고 가라앉아요.
examples.en: Starch doesn't dissolve well in cold water and sinks.

explain: 요리에서는 '감자 전분', '옥수수 전분', '전분 가루'처럼 말하고, 같은 뜻으로 '녹말'도 써요. 영양이나 과학 이야기에서는 탄수화물의 한 종류로 나와요.
explain_en: In cooking it appears as '감자 전분', '옥수수 전분' and '전분 가루', and '녹말' is also used for the same thing. In nutrition and science talk it comes up as a kind of carbohydrate.
